# TCAT Wiki

> Documentation for the open transportation accessibility ecosystem developed by the Taskar Center for Accessible Technology (TCAT) at the University of Washington. TCAT works alongside people with disabilities, public agencies, researchers, advocates, and local communities to co-design data, tools, and standards that improve pedestrian accessibility and mobility. This wiki documents the technologies, datasets, workflows, and community practices that support that mission.

TCAT follows a community-based participatory research and action approach. People with lived experience of disability participate throughout the lifecycle of our work—from identifying priorities and collecting data, to validating results, evaluating tools, and shaping future research. Our goal is not simply to build better routing software, but to create open infrastructure that enables more equitable transportation decision-making.

TCAT develops open-source tools, open standards, and shared data infrastructure that support accessible transportation planning. These resources enable governments, community organizations, researchers, software developers, and residents to collaboratively document pedestrian environments, understand accessibility barriers, and improve mobility for people with disabilities and other nondrivers.

The core dataset is **OS-CONNECT**—a high-resolution, continuously improving connected pedestrian network for Washington State. It is structured using the **OpenSidewalks (OSW)** schema and managed through the **Transportation Data Exchange Initiative (TDEI)** platform, where it can be validated, versioned, shared, and reused by a growing ecosystem of accessibility applications.

## Key Acronyms

- **TCAT** — Taskar Center for Accessible Technology (University of Washington)
- **OSW** — OpenSidewalks: an open standard for pedestrian network data
- **TDEI** — Transportation Data Exchange Initiative: platform and API infrastructure for transportation accessibility data
- **OS-CONNECT** — Washington State's connected pedestrian network dataset, represented using the OpenSidewalks schema
- **ASR** — AVIV ScoutRoute: mobile crowdsourcing application for pedestrian data collection

## How the Ecosystem Works

```
Communities • People with lived experience • Public agencies • Researchers
                                 │
                                 ▼
          Community mapping • Walk audits • Surveys • Validation
                                 │
                                 ▼
      AVIV ScoutRoute • Rapid • JOSM • Prophet • Other data sources
                                 │
                                 ▼
                              TDEI Core
      (validation • metadata • provenance • QA/QC • access control • APIs)
                                 │
                                 ▼
                         Shared Open Data Infrastructure
                                 │
                                 ▼
       AccessMap • Walksheds • Audiom • Conveyal • Research Tools
                                 │
                                 ▼
    Planning • Research • Infrastructure Investment • Community Advocacy
```

This ecosystem is designed to support collaborative stewardship of accessibility data. Community members, advocacy organizations, transportation agencies, researchers, and software developers all contribute to and benefit from shared, openly documented transportation accessibility infrastructure.

---

# Community & Research

TCAT's technologies are developed in partnership with communities, disability advocates, transportation professionals, researchers, and government agencies. The documentation throughout this wiki reflects both the technical implementation of the platform and the collaborative practices used to improve accessibility data over time.

Examples include:

- Community walk audits
- Participatory accessibility mapping
- Mapathons and organized editing events
- Accessibility advisory groups
- Research studies and publications
- Agency implementation guidance
- Community validation workflows

---

# OS-CONNECT

- [OS-CONNECT Overview](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/os-connect/): Community-informed connected pedestrian network for Washington State (320+ cities and counties)
- [OS-CONNECT Data Viewer User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/os-connect/data-viewer/user-manual/): Explore pedestrian accessibility data using an interactive web map (no GIS experience required)
- [QA/QC Reports User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/os-connect/qa-qc/user-manual/): Understand data quality reports used to guide community review and jurisdictional improvement efforts

---

# TDEI

- [TDEI Overview](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/tdei/): Shared platform supporting transportation accessibility data stewardship, publication, APIs, and collaboration
- [TDEI Portal User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/tdei/portal/user-manual/): Account registration, API keys, downloads, publishing workflows, and portal access
- [TDEI Core](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/tdei/tdei-core/): Core infrastructure documentation, validation pipeline, provenance model, and platform architecture

---

# OpenSidewalks Schema

- [OpenSidewalks Overview](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/): Open community standard for representing pedestrian infrastructure and accessibility
- [OpenSidewalks Schema](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/schema/): Data model describing pedestrian networks, including nodes, edges, zones, points, lines, and polygons
- [Core Edges in OSW](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/schema/core-edges-in-osw/): Representing sidewalks, crossings, pathways, and pedestrian connections
- [Custom Points in OSW](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/schema/custom-points-in-osw/): Modeling curb ramps and other accessibility-related point features
- [OpenSidewalks in OSM](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/schema/osw-in-osm/): Contributing OpenSidewalks data through OpenStreetMap
- [OSM US Tasking Manager](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/tasking-manager/): Coordinated community mapping initiatives
- [Tasking Manager Project List](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/opensidewalks/tasking-manager/project-list/): Active and completed collaborative mapping projects

---

# Workspaces & Editing

- [Workspaces Overview](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/workspaces/): Collaborative editing environment supporting agencies, researchers, volunteers, and community members in maintaining pedestrian accessibility datasets
- [Rapid Editor User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/rapid/user-manual/): Editing OpenSidewalks data using the integrated Rapid editor
- [JOSM Settings Guide](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/josm/workspaces-josm-settings/): Configure JOSM for editing datasets within TDEI Workspaces
- [AVIV ScoutRoute User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/aviv-scoutroute/user-manual/): Collect accessibility observations using the AVIV ScoutRoute mobile application
- [AVIV ScoutRoute Quest Definition Guides](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/aviv-scoutroute/quests/): Create and configure structured community data collection workflows

---

# AccessMap & Walksheds

- [AccessMap User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/accessmap/user-manual/): Personalized pedestrian routing based on accessibility preferences, mobility needs, and available infrastructure
- [Walksheds User Manual](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/walksheds/user-manual/): Analyze accessibility, evaluate transportation investments, and prioritize infrastructure improvements under different mobility scenarios

---

# Assistant Knowledge Base (Agent Layer)

Every page on this site is also served as raw Markdown at its docs-relative source path, including its `.md` filename. This is not always the human URL with `.md` appended: human index-page URLs omit `index`, while agent URLs retain it. For example,

`https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/accessmap/`

corresponds to

`https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/accessmap/index.md`

This applies regardless of whether the page has been reviewed for human-facing publication. HTML pages expose a `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` element pointing to the canonical Markdown source so that automated systems can retrieve the appropriate documentation directly.

- [Assistant Knowledge Base — Dispatch](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/assistant/dispatch.md): Registry of all documentation pages available to AI assistants
- [Assistant Knowledge Base Overview](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/assistant/index.md): Purpose and organization of the assistant knowledge base
- [Assistant Knowledge Base Article Schema](https://taskarcenteratuw.github.io/tcat-wiki/assistant/schema.md): Authoring conventions, metadata schema, and human-versus-agent documentation workflow
